item.title: Three by Zito: Avant-garde Fashion Label that lets You Power-dress in Style
item.description:
“Workwear does not have to be boring, and Three by Zito creates pieces that are different and a breath of fresh air.” Tzipora, founder and designer behind Three by Zito

Source: https://sparyn.com/imprint/three-by-zito-avant-garde-fashion-power-dress-in-style/ Author: sparyn Published: 2021-10-05T22:00:00.000Z Read time: 3 mins read

Contrary to popular belief, workwear can be fun and stylish. Thanks to the emerging culture of creativity and self-expression, many companies have loosened up their restrictions on workplace fashion. Most clothing boutiques have advertised their pieces of corporate attire as very plain and formal, but Three by Zito is leading a new trend of workwear that’s chic and sustainable.

item.title: Packaging design brief — what to send your 3PL before production
item.description:
A beautiful unboxing mockup in Figma means nothing if the warehouse receives low-res logos and no dielines. Here is the minimum packaging design brief Tendlyn needs to kit correctly on day one.

Assets checklist

  1. Vector logo (SVG/AI/PDF)—not a low-res screenshot from your website or store theme
  2. Mailer/box dielines with bleed and panel labels
  3. Color specs (Pantone or CMYK) for tissue, tape, and cards
  4. Insert copy—thank-you card, warranty, QR to review page
  5. Kitting map—which SKU gets which insert in multi-item orders

Unboxing sequence

Document the order of operations: product wrap → tissue → card → sticker seal. Warehouses default to fastest pick path unless you specify brand sequence.

item.title: Landed cost math every China buyer should run before signing a PO
item.description:
The factory sent a quote that looks 40% below your current supplier. Before you celebrate, run landed cost math—or you will discover the gap in QC rework, air freight panic, and chargebacks.

The formula (simplified)

Landed cost per unit ≈

(Factory unit price + QC + packaging + inland China logistics + international freight + duties/taxes + defect reserve) ÷ sellable units

Line items buyers forget

Cost bucket Why it matters
MOQ overbuy 3,000 units when you sell 200/month ties up cash for 15 months
PSI & rework Cheap units that fail inspection still cost handling time
Branded packaging Mailers and inserts are marketing—not optional for D2C
Last-mile speed Air freight fixes a late factory but kills margin
Defect reserve Plan 1–3% write-off even with good QC

How Tendlyn uses this in sourcing

We quote delivered-to-warehouse or DDP-style scenarios when clients share target markets—so you compare suppliers on outcome, not factory FOB alone.

item.title: AQL sampling explained for D2C brand owners
item.description:
Acceptable Quality Limit (AQL) is the statistical backbone of most pre-shipment inspections. It balances cost and coverage—so you are not paying to inspect every unit on a 10,000-piece order.

How AQL works in plain language

Inspectors pull a random sample based on order size and inspect against your defect criteria. If defects exceed the agreed limit, the batch fails—full stop.

Inspection level Best for
General II (default) Most consumer D2C SKUs
General III Higher-risk electronics or safety items
100% inspection Low volume, high ticket, or new factory relationship

item.title: How to spot a trading company posing as a factory
item.description:
Trading companies are not always malicious— but when they pose as manufacturers, you pay middleman margins and lose control of production timing, QC, and export documentation.

Five red flags before you wire a deposit

  1. No production floor in video calls — only showrooms or sample rooms.
  2. Business license category does not include manufacturing scope.
  3. MOQ flexibility that is too good — real factories have line minimums.
  4. Refusal of third-party audit or “audit not allowed during peak season.”
  5. Export history that cannot be verified with reference buyers.

What a real audit reveals

Tendlyn auditors photograph production lines, QC stations, raw material storage, and export packing areas—not staged sample rooms. We cross-check license data against the entity on the contract and the bank account receiving your deposit.

item.title: Global fulfillment onboarding — a 48-hour warehouse-to-doorstep guide
item.description:
Branded global dropshipping from a China-based hub should not mean scattered vendors and WeChat screenshots. Tendlyn’s fulfillment stack handles order handoff, pick-pack-ship, and tracking—so you focus on growth, not logistics ops.

Onboarding checklist

  1. SKU mapping — align your product catalog to warehouse bin IDs and kitting rules.
  2. Inventory staging — QC-cleared stock positioned for dispatch readiness.
  3. Lane rules — EU vs. US service levels and carrier selection per SKU weight class.
  4. Order handoff — confirm how orders flow from your team to our warehouse operations.
  5. Tracking visibility — carrier events shared with your team and customer notifications.

The 24–48 hour dispatch target

Orders confirmed before the daily cut-off enter pick-pack-ship the same or next business day, depending on kitting complexity.

item.title: Branded packaging ROI — why unboxing drives repeat D2C orders
item.description:
Generic poly mailers signal “dropship junk” the moment a customer opens the door. Branded packaging is one of the highest-ROI upgrades in cross-border D2C—because it costs pennies per unit but moves repeat rate and UGC.

What premium kitting includes

  • Custom mailers and tissue with your palette and logo
  • Thank-you cards and insert offers (referral, review, warranty)
  • Branded stickers and tamper seals
  • Multi-SKU bundles assembled in our central warehouse

Storage + kitting in one account

Tendlyn holds inventory securely, then picks, kits, and ships when your order is confirmed—no separate 3PL handoff.

item.title: Pre-shipment inspection 101 — stop bad reviews before they ship
item.description:
Shipping blind is the fastest way to turn a five-star brand into a chargeback machine. Pre-shipment inspection (PSI) is your last defensible gate before goods leave China.

The PSI workflow

  1. AQL sampling — statistical or 100% inspection based on SKU risk and order value.
  2. Functional testing — power-on, dimension checks, and packaging drop tests where relevant.
  3. Cosmetic grading — surface defects sorted against your accept/reject matrix.
  4. HD evidence — timestamped photos and video clips tied to carton IDs.
  5. Hold / release — nothing ships until you approve the report in writing.

Defect sorting and rework

When issues appear, Tendlyn coordinates sorting, rework, or partial shipment—so you choose whether to absorb delay or protect your review score.

item.title: The 12-point factory audit checklist every overseas buyer needs
item.description:
Overseas buyers lose months—and sometimes entire product lines—when a “factory” turns out to be a trading desk or a facility that cannot hit quoted MOQs. Tendlyn’s on-site audits follow a 12-point checklist before any PO is signed.

What we verify on the ground

  1. Business registration — legal entity matches export documentation.
  2. Production capacity — line count, shifts, and realistic throughput vs. your volume.
  3. Equipment inventory — machines match the SKU category you are buying.
  4. QC station — incoming, in-process, and outbound checkpoints exist and are staffed.
  5. Sample room — retained units and revision history for traceability.
  6. Export history — reference buyers and destination markets, not just screenshots.
  7. Certification wall — CE, RoHS, ISO, or category-specific certs with valid dates.
  8. Sub-supplier map — who actually makes critical components.
  9. Labor & ethics snapshot — basic social compliance signals for brand risk.
  10. Financial stability — red flags that predict mid-production ghosting.
  11. Communication layer — English-capable engineering contact, not just sales chat.
  12. Pilot readiness — sample lead time, tooling deposits, and revision policy in writing.

Why this matters for D2C brands

When you dropship blind, you inherit every factory lie your supplier never corrected. An independent audit gives you negotiation leverage, realistic lead times, and a paper trail if disputes arise.
